Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.dataWeReadBody: With your permission, we read your register's sales, order, catalog, staff and timecard data (read-only — we can never change anything or move your money). We also store the costs, bills, receipts and bank lines you give us.
Privacy.dataWeNeverTouchBody: We never ask for your bank or register password. We never see your customers' card numbers. We never move money or place orders on your behalf.
Privacy.howWeProtectItBody: Register connection tokens are encrypted at rest. Uploaded files are private to your business. We never log tokens, bank lines, or receipt images.
Privacy.aiUseBody: We use AI to read receipts, categorize bank statement lines, and parse voice entries you record. Only the data needed for that task is sent, never your customers' names or card numbers.
Privacy.yourControlBody: You can review, correct, or remove any cost we've recorded. You can disconnect your register at any time from Settings.
Privacy.deletingYourAccountBody: Deleting your account permanently removes your business data and files, and disconnects any connected register. This can't be undone.

ProcessingFees.processedSalesShareHint: For example, enter 80 if about 80% of café sales are card payments through this processor.
ProcessingFees.processedTransactionShare: Share of transactions paid through this processor
ProcessingFees.processedTransactionShareHint: Advanced only. Use this when the share of card transactions is meaningfully different from the share of card sales.
ProcessingFees.averageTicketHint: Only needed when a fixed per-payment fee applies and AI Cafe does not have trustworthy real order counts.
ProcessingFees.rulesHint: Use this only if your processor charges different rates for different payment types. Sales mix and transaction mix should each total 100% across the rules.
ProcessingFees.saved: Fallback estimate saved. Actual connected or imported fees will still take priority automatically.
ProcessingFees.incompleteWarning: Complete the highlighted fee details before saving.
ProcessingFees.actualCoverage: Actual fees on {actual} of {sales} sales days
ProcessingFees.completeActualCoverage: Your recent sales days are fully covered by actual processing fees. You do not need an estimate right now.
ProcessingFees.missingCoverage: {count} recent sales days still need processing-fee coverage.
ProcessingFees.actualFirstNote: If your register or fee report gives AI Cafe the fee that was actually charged, that amount is used automatically. An estimate never adds on top of an actual fee.
ProcessingFees.estimateIntro: Use this only for days where AI Cafe cannot get the actual fee. The simple setup covers most cafés; advanced settings are only for multiple rate types.
ProcessingFees.processorHelp: Who charges the card-processing fee. AI Cafe fills this from a connected register when it can. This label identifies the source of the fallback estimate; it does not change your POS.
ProcessingFees.effectiveFromHelp: The first date this fee agreement applies. This keeps an old rate from being applied after your processor changes pricing, and keeps a new rate from rewriting older history.
ProcessingFees.processedSalesShareHelp: This is not the fee rate. It is the portion of total café sales that goes through this processor. Cash and payments handled elsewhere should not be included. In the simple setup AI Cafe uses the same share for transaction count; Advanced lets you separate them.
ProcessingFees.processedTransactionShareHelp: Fixed per-payment fees depend on how many transactions used the processor, not only on sales dollars. Keep this separate only when you know the transaction mix differs from the sales mix.
ProcessingFees.averageTicketHelp: AI Cafe uses this only to estimate the number of processed payments when real order counts are unavailable. If connected POS order counts are trustworthy, this field is ignored.
ProcessingFees.orderCountsAutomatic: AI Cafe has trustworthy real order counts for {count} recent sales days, so it can use those automatically for fixed per-payment fees.
ProcessingFees.percentageRateHelp: The percentage your processor charges on processed sales. Example: 2.6% means about $2.60 for every $100 processed.
ProcessingFees.fixedFeeHelp: A flat amount charged for each processed payment, such as $0.10. AI Cafe uses real order counts when available instead of asking you to guess transaction volume.
ProcessingFees.salesMixHelp: Advanced only. If you have multiple rate types, this tells AI Cafe what share of processed sales uses this particular rate. All rate rules together should total 100%.
ProcessingFees.transactionMixHelp: Advanced only. If you have multiple rate types, this tells AI Cafe what share of processed payment count uses this rate. All rate rules together should total 100%.
ProcessingFees.advancedHint: Only open this if you have different rates for different cards, online payments, or other payment types.

Economics.title: Profit goal simulator
Economics.subtitle: Try a profit target and see a pricing-only what-if. Nothing is saved or changed in your POS.

Economics.targetMarginHint: Enter the operating margin you want to explore. This simulation does not become a saved business setting.

Economics.assumption: This asks what prices could look like if pricing alone had to support the target, assuming sales volume, staffing, recipes, and running costs stay the same.
Economics.readyMeetsTarget: Your current operating margin already meets this target. AI Cafe does not suggest lowering existing prices to move the café back down to the target.
Economics.readyNeedsIncrease: To reach {target} through pricing alone, average menu prices would need to rise about {increase}, assuming the same sales volume.
Economics.largeChange: This is a large pricing change. It may be more realistic to combine pricing with labor, product-cost, menu-mix, or overhead improvements rather than rely on prices alone.
Economics.unavailableSales: At least 7 sales days are needed before AI Cafe runs this business-wide pricing simulation.
Economics.unavailableFees: Processing fees are incomplete, so the simulator would overstate profit. Add actual fees or confirm an estimate first.
Economics.unavailableCosts: Some sold menu items are missing product costs, so the simulator would overstate profit.
Economics.unavailableOperating: Add or confirm the missing monthly operating costs (rent, bills and supplies) before AI CAFE can calculate a reliable operating margin or run this price simulation.
Economics.targetNotFeasible: This target is not feasible from the current cost structure through pricing alone.
